articles.summary: Are the UK and EU about to sign a deal to scrap post-Brexit red tape?
articles.body: Today, the UK and EU have agreed a draft deal on removing post-Brexit checks ahead of the UK-EU summit later this month. articles.title: Lei Aldir Blanc em Parauapebas: inscrições prorrogadas até 6/11 | G1
articles.standfirst: Oportunidades são destinadas a projetos de criação, formação e circulação cultural. Interessados devem consultar os editais e os critérios de participação nos canais oficiais da prefeitura.
articles.summary: A Prefeitura de Parauapebas prorrogou o prazo dos editais da Lei Aldir Blanc para projetos de criação, formação e circulação, com inscrições abertas até 6 de novembro.
articles.body:
Inscrições para editais culturais da Lei Aldir Blanc são prorrogadas até 6 de novembro em Parauapebas — Foto: Divulgação

Artistas, produtores e trabalhadores da cultura de Parauapebas, no sudeste do Pará, têm até sexta-feira (6) para se inscrever em três editais da Política Nacional Aldir Blanc (PNAB) de 2026. O prazo foi prorrogado pela prefeitura, conforme publicação no Diário Oficial do Município desta terça-feira (3).

As oportunidades são voltadas a projetos culturais em diferentes modalidades, incluindo criação artística, atividades de formação e circulação de produções culturais.

Quais editais estão com inscrições abertas?

Os interessados podem apresentar propostas em três modalidades:

Edital nº 003/2026 – Projetos Culturais de Criação: destinado a projetos de criação cultural.

Edital nº 004/2026 – Projetos de Formação Cultural: voltado a propostas de formação na área cultural.

Edital nº 005/2026 – Projetos de Circulação: destinado a projetos de circulação cultural.

Cada edital possui orientações e critérios próprios, que devem ser consultados antes da inscrição.

Os interessados devem acessar os canais oficiais da Prefeitura de Parauapebas e da Secretaria Municipal de Cultura (Secult) para consultar os editais, os cronogramas atualizados e as orientações de participação.

O comunicado não detalha o procedimento de inscrição nem os valores destinados a cada modalidade.

6 de novembro: último dia para inscrições.

11 a 17 de novembro: seleção e análise dos projetos pela banca avaliadora.

19 e 20 de novembro: divulgação dos resultados preliminares.

27 de novembro: divulgação do resultado final.

A prorrogação dos prazos foi publicada na edição nº 1474 do Diário Oficial do Município, em 3 de novembro de 2026.

Os projetos inscritos serão analisados por uma banca avaliadora, conforme os critérios estabelecidos em cada edital. O resultado final está previsto para 27 de novembro.

articles.title: Pedreiro morre ao cair em poço aberto para construção de elevador  | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo consta no boletim de ocorrência, o acidente ocorreu nesta terça-feira (3) em São José do Rio Preto (SP).
articles.summary: Um pedreiro de 75 anos morreu na manhã desta terça-feira (3) em São José do Rio Preto (SP) ao cair em um poço destinado à construção de um elevador em uma obra.
articles.body:
Deinter 5 - São José do Rio Preto (SP) — Foto: Google Street View

Um pedreiro de 75 anos morreu na manhã desta terça-feira (3) em São José do Rio Preto (SP) ao cair em um poço destinado à construção de um elevador em uma obra.

Segundo consta no boletim de ocorrência, José Amorim da Silva estava na área superior do prédio junto com outro trabalhador, quando teria tropeçado em ferragens existentes no local, perdido o equilíbrio e caído no poço.

O operário que viu o momento do acidente contou aos demais trabalhadores que José caminhava de costas no momento em que ocorreu a queda. Uma equipe do Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) foi acionada e constatou o óbito do pedreiro no local.

À TV TEM, o Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego (MTE) informou que, até a última atualização desta reportagem, o acidente não havia sido registrado no sistema. A reportagem tenta contato com a construtora responsável pela obra.

O boletim de ocorrência foi registrado como morte suspeita / morte acidental.

articles.title: Eleições nos EUA: Qual é o partido de Donald Trump? | G1
articles.standfirst: As eleições de meio de mandato movimentam a política americana nesta terça-feira (3), com disputas por vagas no Congresso e governos estaduais.
articles.summary: As eleições de meio de mandato movimentam a política americana nesta terça-feira (3), com disputas por vagas no Congresso e governos estaduais.
articles.body:
As eleições de meio de mandato dos Estados Unidos ( midterms ) acontecem nesta terça-feira (3) e colocam em disputa vagas no Congresso e governos estaduais. Em meio à votação, uma das dúvidas mais pesquisadas sobre a política americana é a qual partido pertence o presidente Donald Trump . O atual presidente dos EUA é filiado ao Partido Republicano , uma das duas principais forças políticas do país.

Trump representa o partido desde que voltou à disputa pela Casa Branca, em 2024. Ele também foi o candidato republicano nas eleições presidenciais de 2016, quando conquistou seu primeiro mandato. Atualmente, ocupa novamente a Presidência dos Estados Unidos, cargo que assumiu em janeiro de 2025.

Qual é a diferença entre republicanos e democratas?

O Partido Republicano e o Partido Democrata são as duas principais legendas da política americana e concentram a maior parte da representação no Congresso e das disputas presidenciais.

Os republicanos, partido de Trump, são tradicionalmente associados a posições conservadoras. Já o Partido Democrata reúne diferentes correntes políticas, incluindo grupos liberais e progressistas.

As duas legendas disputam espaço nas eleições legislativas e presidenciais, além de cargos estaduais e locais.

Presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump. — Foto: Nathan Howard/Reuters

O que está em disputa nas eleições dos EUA?

As eleições desta terça-feira (3) são as chamadas eleições de meio de mandato, conhecidas como midterms. Elas acontecem na metade do período presidencial e não incluem uma disputa pela Presidência.

Neste ano, os americanos votam para renovar todas as 435 cadeiras da Câmara dos Representantes e 35 das 100 vagas do Senado. Também há eleições para governador em 36 estados, além de consultas sobre temas locais.

O resultado pode alterar a composição do Congresso e, consequentemente, a relação de forças entre o governo Trump e a oposição democrata.

Como o presidente pertence ao Partido Republicano, o desempenho da legenda nas urnas também é acompanhado como um indicador do apoio político ao governo durante seu segundo mandato

articles.title: Nove são denunciados por desvio de R$ 5 milhões do Fundeb e SUS no PI | G1
articles.standfirst: Denúncia envolve empresários, agentes públicos e antiga servidora; MPF pediu bloqueio de bens para tentar recuperar recursos supostamente desviados.
articles.summary: Denúncia envolve empresários, agentes públicos e antiga servidora; MPF pediu bloqueio de bens para tentar recuperar recursos supostamente desviados.
articles.body:
Ministério Público Federal do Piauí — Foto: Andrê Nascimento/ G1 PI

Nove pessoas foram denunciadas à Justiça Federal por suspeita de participar de um esquema de fraudes em licitações e desvio de recursos públicos no Piauí. Segundo o Ministério Público Federal (MPF), o grupo teria causado prejuízo superior a R$ 4,9 milhões em verbas do Fundo de Manutenção e Desenvolvimento da Educação Básica (Fundeb) e do Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS).

De acordo com a denúncia apresentada no âmbito da Operação Holding, os investigados desviavam recursos federais, direcionavam contratos públicos e pagavam propina a agentes públicos.

Segundo o MPF, o grupo utilizava empresas registradas em nome de terceiros para esconder os verdadeiros responsáveis pelo esquema e dificultar a fiscalização dos órgãos de controle.

De acordo com a investigação, os editais eram elaborados com exigências que limitavam a participação de concorrentes. O grupo também apresentava propostas previamente combinadas para simular disputa entre empresas.

O MPF afirma ainda que parte dos recursos sacados era usada para o pagamento de propina a agentes públicos.

As supostas irregularidades foram identificadas em licitações para contratação de serviços terceirizados e de limpeza pública nos municípios de Francinópolis, Manoel Emídio e Colônia do Gurguéia.

Entre as práticas apontadas pela investigação estão a entrega antecipada de propostas a agentes públicos e o compartilhamento de máquinas e equipamentos entre municípios. Segundo o MPF, isso era feito para criar a impressão de que contratos diferentes estavam sendo executados de forma independente.

Entre os denunciados estão empresários, gestores municipais, engenheiros, profissionais das áreas jurídica e contábil, agentes públicos e uma servidora municipal que ocupava cargo de chefia em uma Secretaria de Administração e Obras.

Conforme a participação atribuída a cada investigado, eles foram denunciados por crimes como associação criminosa , fraude em licitações e contratos públicos , corrupção ativa e passiva , peculato-desvio e falsidade ideológica .

Para tentar recuperar os recursos supostamente desviados, o MPF pediu à Justiça o bloqueio de bens, veículos e valores dos investigados.

O órgão também solicitou a suspensão de contratos ainda vigentes entre as empresas investigadas e o município, a perda do cargo da servidora denunciada e o envio do processo a órgãos responsáveis pela apuração de possíveis infrações disciplinares.

*Yngridy Vieira, estagiária sob supervisão de Ilanna Serena.

articles.title: Eleições nos EUA: Senado pode ter primeiro muçulmano de sua história | G1
articles.standfirst: 'Outsider' democrata, Abdul El-Sayed é favorito na corrida para o Senado no Michigan, estado decisivo nas midterms. Médico de 42 anos, El-Sayed é filho de egípcios e nascido nos EUA. Durante a campanha, enfrentou uma onda de críticas e questionamentos por sua religião.
articles.summary: 'Outsider' democrata, Abdul El-Sayed lidera corrida para o Senado no Michigan, estado decisivo nas midterms. Médico de 42 anos, El-Sayed é filho de egípcios e nascido nos EUA.
articles.body:
O candidato democrata ao Senado pelo Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed, atrás de uma bandeira dos Estados Unidos em ato de campanha em Mount Clemens, no Michigan, em 31 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Julia Demaree Nikhinson/ AP

Se as pesquisas se confirmarem, os Estados Unidos podem ter o primeiro senador muçulmano de sua história. Trata-se de Abdul El-Sayed, médico democrata "outsider" do estado do Michigan que se tornou um dos grandes nomes da campanha das midterms , as eleições que renovam parte do Legislativo dos Estados Unidos.

El-Sayed, de 42 anos, viralizou nas redes sociais, ganhou a companhia do ex-presidente Barack Obama na reta final da campanha e virou uma das principais estrelas do Partido Democrata.

Nascido nos arredores de Detroit, nos EUA, e filho de egípcios, El-Sayed integra a ala mais progressista do partido . Venceu as primárias a despeito do núcleo duro da sigla, que preferia seu rival. Agora, no entanto, pesquisas de intenção de voto projetam vitória por uma margem de entre 3 e 7 pontos percentuais para o candidato no Michigan, estado decisivo na eleição para o Senado.

➡️ Projeções indicam que os democratas, partido de oposição a Trump, devem retomar o controle da Câmara e podem conquistar maioria no Senado — atualmente, o Partido Republicano, do presidente dos EUA, detém o controle nas duas Casas.

O ex-presidente dos EUA, Barack Obama, faz campanha com o candidato democrata ao Senado dos EUA, Abdul El- Sayed , e a candidata democrata ao governo, Jocelyn Benson, em Detroit, Michigan — Foto: REUTERS/Rebecca Cook

Casado com a psiquiatra Sarah Jukaku, de origem indiana e também muçulmana, El-Sayed não colocou a religião na pauta de sua campanha, mas virou alvo de constantes questionamentos e ataques à sua fé.

Em desses questionamentos, durante um comício, ele disse que é apenas "um candidato ao Senado que, por acaso, é muçulmano". E passou sua campanha tentando voltas as atenções para pautas de saúde, o eixo central de sua campanha — o democrata defende uma proposta de saúde universal para todos os cidadãos dos EUA financiada pelo governo, além da eliminação de dívidas médicas.

O democrata estudou biologia e ciência política e, depois, migrou para a faculdade de medicina em Columbia. Completou os estudos com um doutorado em saúde pública na Universidade de Oxford, no Reino Unido.

O candidato ao Senado do Michigan Abdul El-Sayed ao lado de sua esposa, Sarah Jukaku, durante ato de campanha em Detroit, em 2 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Julia Demaree Nikhinson/ AP

Após voltar aos EUA, foi professor de epidemiologia na Universidade de Columbia e dirigiu o Departamento de Saúde de Detroit, onde vive com a esposa e as duas filhas do casal — na reta final de campanha, lançou um anúncio no qual se apresenta como um pai amoroso de duas filhas.

Mas, apesar da formação e da experiência na área de saúde, começou a tentar migrar para a política em 2018, quando foi pré-candidato ao governo por Michigan, mas perdeu nas primárias democratas.

Agora, como o grande nome de seu partido no Michigan, enfrentará o republicano Mike Rogers, ex-deputado federal, no que pode se tornar a disputa mais acirrada deste ano por uma cadeira no Senado atualmente ocupada pelos democratas.

Rogers tem tentado explorar dúvidas entre eleitores negros e, principalmente judeus, que se dividiram após duras críticas de El-Sayed ao apoio do governo dos Estados Unidos a Israel. O republicano retratou El-Sayed como um candidato de pauta única, "mais focado em Gaza do que em Michigan" .

articles.title: Aumento de chuvas e calor reacende alerta para avanço da dengue em SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Dados do Liraa apontam 7 cidades da região de Bauru (SP) em situação de risco e outras 25 em estado de alerta. Lins (SP) lidera índice até a última atualização nesta segunda-feira (2).
articles.summary: Devido à dengue no interior de SP, cidades como Lins e Bauru entram em alerta após levantamento apontar alto risco de infestação por larvas do Aedes aegypti.
articles.body:
O aumento das chuvas combinado às altas temperaturas reacendeu a preocupação com a proliferação do mosquito Aedes aegypti no interior de São Paulo.

Dados da Secretaria de Estado da Saúde (SES) apontam que, das 52 cidades que enviaram relatórios ao Departamento Regional de Saúde (DRS) de Bauru até a última segunda-feira (2), sete entraram em situação de risco e outras 25 estão em estado de alerta para epidemia de dengue.

Aumento de chuvas e calor reacende alerta para avanço da dengue no interior de SP — Foto: TV TEM/Reprodução

O diagnóstico consta no Levantamento Rápido de Índices para Aedes aegypti (Liraa) referente a outubro.

O cálculo é feito com base no Índice de Infestação Predial (IIP), parâmetro do Ministério da Saúde que classifica como risco de surto qualquer localidade onde mais de 4% dos imóveis pesquisados apresentem larvas do vetor transmissor da dengue, zika e chikungunya.

Entre os municípios monitorados, Lins (SP) registrou o cenário mais preocupante da região, com IIP de 7,06%. De acordo com a secretária municipal de Saúde, Silvia Cardoso, os trabalhos de combate a criadouros são permanentes, mas a recusa de moradores para vistorias nas residências ainda é o principal obstáculo enfrentado pelos agentes de combate a endemias.

"Nós tivemos 13 casos positivos de dengue este ano, sendo o último confirmado em junho. Esse indicador de infestação rápida larvária é importante para direcionarmos ações, como o controle mecânico de criadouros. Sem dúvida, não é o único índice, precisamos do apoio da população. Tivemos alterações climáticas que interferem diretamente, mas que não estão sozinhas na infestação do mosquito", afirmou a secretária.

Aedes aegypti, mosquito transmissor da dengue — Foto: g1

Além de Lins, outras seis cidades da região ultrapassaram o teto de 4% do Ministério da Saúde e figuram na faixa de risco:

Os órgãos de vigilância epidemiológica reforçam a necessidade de eliminar pratos sob vasos de plantas, garrafas destampadas, recipientes plásticos e calhas obstruídas, evitando o acúmulo de água parada no período de chuvas frequentes

articles.body:

Nona grava audiovisual com Dilsinho em Aracaju — Foto: Antônio Walter

"Estou vivendo um sonho! Dilsinho é uma das minhas maiores referências musicais, um artista que admiro muito e que sempre acompanhei", afirmou Nona.

Dilsinho também destacou a identificação com o cantor sergipano e a repercussão de seu trabalho. “O som de Nona já tinha chegado ao Sudeste. Conheci o artista em setembro, durante uma apresentação aqui em Aracaju, e, senti vontade de chamá-lo ao palco naquele momento", disse.

Segundo a assessoria de comunicação de Nona, a música e o audiovisual com Dilsinho devem ser lançados em breve nas plataformas digitais.

articles.title: Estrada do Piripau: obra atrasa e novo prazo é para 2027 em Ribeirão | G1
articles.standfirst: Pavimentação deveria ter sido concluída em setembro, mas ainda faltam 20% dos serviços. Segundo o DER, serviço só deve ser terminado em março de 2027.
articles.summary: A pavimentação da Estrada do Piripau em Ribeirão Preto segue inacabada e, após revisões no projeto, o DER estendeu o prazo de conclusão para março de 2027.
articles.body:
A obra de pavimentação da Estrada do Piripau , na zona Leste de Ribeirão Preto (SP), está atrasada e ainda causa transtornos a motoristas e moradores que precisam passar diariamente pelo local . Com investimento de R$ 11,3 milhões do governo estadual, os serviços ao longo de 6,6 quilômetros deveriam ter sido concluídos em setembro deste ano, mas ainda faltam 20% para a entrega.

Também conhecida como Avenida Alfredo Ravanelli, a estrada tem trechos asfaltados separados por um longo percurso de terra, onde motoristas enfrentam poeira nos dias secos e lama nos períodos de chuva.

A situação é a mesma registrada em abril deste ano, quando uma reportagem da EPTV , afiliada da TV Globo, mostrou os problemas enfrentados por quem utiliza a via. Sete meses depois, o trecho continua sem pavimentação.

Estrada do Piripau tem trecho de aproximadamente 1,3 quilômetro sem asfalto em Ribeirão Preto, SP — Foto: Luciano Tolentino/EPTV

A via dá acesso a chácaras e ranchos localizados às margens do Rio Pardo.

Os aposentados Ângela Leite e José Carlos Leite passam diariamente pela estrada e convivem com as dificuldades provocadas pela falta de asfalto.

José Carlos questiona por que parte do trajeto permanece sem pavimentação, mesmo com outros trechos já concluídos.

“Pela lógica, eles teriam que começar vindo da cidade, de lá para cá, eles começaram do meio para o fim”, questiona o morador.

De acordo com as placas instaladas no local, a obra começou em 16 de abril de 2025 e prevê a pavimentação de mais de 6,6 quilômetros da estrada.

Estrada do Piripau tem trecho de 1,3 quilômetro de terra e lama em Ribeirão Preto, SP — Foto: Luciano Tolentino/EPTV

O prazo inicial de execução era de 12 meses, mas foi ampliado para 17 meses, com conclusão prevista para setembro de 2026. Mesmo com a prorrogação, os serviços não foram finalizados.

Enquanto a pavimentação não é concluída, os motoristas precisam deixar o asfalto, atravessar o trecho de terra e voltar à parte pavimentada.

A falta de continuidade da obra é motivo de reclamação entre os moradores, que cobram uma solução definitiva para a estrada.

“Antigamente eles faziam a manutenção da estrada e nem isso fazem mais hoje. Quando chove, eles vêm, passam a patrola, jogam a terra da lateral para o meio da estrada. Aí a primeira chuva que dá já leva tudo aquilo lá e formam os buracos de novo. Nós estamos abandonados aqui”, diz José Carlos.

Bairros da zona Leste, próximo à Estrada do Piripau, em Ribeirão Preto, SP — Foto: Luciano Tolentino/EPTV

Procurada, a Prefeitura de Ribeirão Preto disse que o andamento das obras da Estrada do Piripau foi impactado pela necessidade de correções no projeto executado pelo Departamento de Estradas de Rodagem (DER).

Segundo a prefeitura, o projeto revisado foi recebido em abril deste ano, o que exigiu novos procedimentos técnicos e administrativos.

Pesquisas de opinião e agregadores de projeções apontam que o Partido Democrata é favorito na disputa pela Câmara. As projeções indicam que a legenda deve conquistar mais de 230 cadeiras.

Caso as projeções se confirmem, o Partido Republicano, do presidente Donald Trump, perderá o controle da Casa. Nas eleições de 2024, os republicanos conquistaram 220 cadeiras.

Diferentemente do Brasil, o Congresso dos Estados Unidos é renovado parcialmente a cada dois anos. Quando ocorrem na metade do mandato presidencial, essas eleições são chamadas de midterms, ou eleições de meio de mandato.

Os deputados norte-americanos têm mandatos de dois anos, enquanto os senadores têm mandatos de seis anos.

Com isso, a cada dois anos, o país renova toda a Câmara dos Representantes e cerca de um terço do Senado.

articles.title: Austin tech founder killed with wife and children in Florida jet crash had reached a $10M business milestone
articles.summary: Adam Robinson's final LinkedIn post celebrated RB2B hitting $10 million in annual recurring revenue and teased a live debate he would never attend.
articles.body:
An Austin tech founder who was killed alongside his wife and two young children in a fiery Florida jet crash had just celebrated a major business milestone and was making plans for a live event Tuesday in what became his final LinkedIn post.

Adam Robinson, 45, his wife, Helen Sharp, 40, and their children, Emma, 4, and Charlie, 2, were among nine people killed Sunday when the Learjet 60 carrying them from Austin to North Eleuthera in the Bahamas plunged into a Palm Beach County neighborhood.

On the day of the crash, Robinson wrote that RB2B had reached $10 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR).

"RB2B is $10m ARR with 1 FTE," Robinson wrote. "MoltSets is almost $1m ARR."

Two months earlier, Robinson said RB2B was generating $9.5 million in annual recurring revenue and described reaching $10 million with a small team as "the promised land."

Robinson was CEO and co-founder of Retention.com , an Austin-based company that helps businesses identify people who visit their websites and reach them with advertising and marketing.

The company later launched RB2B, which helps businesses identify potential customers visiting their websites. Robinson also led MoltSets, which provides business contact information, including work emails and phone numbers.

In his final post, Robinson described a debate with friend Jesse Ouellette over whether RB2B and MoltSets should remain separate or be combined.

Robinson wrote that Ouellette believed combining them could reduce customer turnover and double revenue, while he favored keeping the products separate.

"My question: WHY DO I NEED TO DO EITHER OF THOSE THINGS?" Robinson wrote.

"Honestly, I'd be thrilled if RB2B never grew another dollar," he added.

The two planned to settle their disagreement during a live debate Tuesday on "Claude Did What!!??"

"So we're settling it LIVE," Robinson wrote.

"There's much more to his argument, but I'm saving it for Tuesday," he added. "Grab some popcorn and pick a side."

The Robinson family was remembered in a joint statement provided to Fox News Digital.

" Adam and Helen were devoted parents , and Emma, 4, and Charlie, 2, were the light of their lives. Helen and Adam were the love affair that will last forever," the families said.

"Their warmth, generosity and gift for making people feel welcome touched so many lives. Their loss will be felt deeply by all those who loved them and who they loved in return."

Retention.com, RB2B and MoltSets also remembered Robinson as "a friend, a mentor and a bold, outspoken leader who lived life to the fullest."

"He cared deeply about the people around him and brought energy and conviction to everything he built," the companies said. "His loss is deeply felt across our team and the tech community, as we collectively mourn this significant loss."

The Learjet departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport at about 10:37 a.m. Sunday with two crew members and seven passengers aboard.

The crew reported light clear ice and moderate turbulence at about 35,000 feet before requesting permission to climb to 37,000 feet. Less than 30 seconds after the request was approved, the crew reported they were descending and issued a mayday call.

Federal investigators said Monday that weather conditions are a major focus of the investigation and that there are indications the aircraft began breaking apart before impact.

The cause of the crash has not been determined.

articles.summary: Gordon Bird was "shocked" after checking tracking data online and discovering the phallic shape.

The service that provides air support to the police has denied deliberately drawing a penis-like shape in the sky via a helicopter's flight path.

Gordon Bird, 53, who lives in Ancells Farm, in Fleet, Hampshire, said his two-year-old daughter was woken up at about 23:00 GMT on Monday by a helicopter flying overhead in multiple circles for at least 15 minutes.

He said he was "shocked" after checking its tracking data online and discovering the phallic shape.

But the National Police Air Service (NPAS) told the BBC that the crew was "orbiting the locations they were directed to as part of the search for a vehicle that had failed to stop for police".

According to tracking data, the police helicopter made the main part of the outline above Blackbushe Airport before circling over Ancells Farm, and then heading back to its base at Redhill.

"I happened to have my computer on, I hadn't gone to bed, so I just looked it up on the tracking," Bird explained.

"The actual buzzing around our estate lasted for 15 or 20 minutes, the actual drawing of the phallus... took about half an hour, and the overall flight, as per flight radar type websites, show it as being an hour."

Bird said when helicopters fly over his house it "vibrates" and the windows "rattle".

"I'm not angry, I am upset at the waste of resources," he said.

NPAS provides aerial support to police forces across England and Wales.

In an email to Bird, it said it understood the "frustration" of having his young daughter "disrupted" by the airborne activity and it was "unfortunate that the flight path shown on public tracking apps resembles a particular shape".

The service told the BBC that on the night in question, its crew had been carrying out checks of "specific roads, junctions and areas identified by officers on the ground".

It said NPAS flights "do not follow defined or predetermined flight plans as they, by their very nature, are dynamic and respond to ever changing, and unpredictable, circumstances on the ground".

"The flight was conducted for a legitimate policing purpose, in support of Thames Valley Police," it added.

articles.title: Israel political deadlock leaves Netanyahu’s future hanging in the balance
articles.summary: With neither bloc near a majority, Arab and ultra-Orthodox parties hold the key to Israel’s next government..
articles.body:
Israel’s election results are due to be certified on Wednesday, but with both leading blocs falling short of a parliamentary majority, negotiations remain deadlocked.

As things stand, the right-wing coalition of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu secured 53 seats in the October 27 vote, while the self-styled Zionist opposition alliance led by former army chief Gadi Eisenkot had 48. A majority requires 61 seats in the 120-strong Knesset. The 19 remaining seats went to the two Arab-led lists – the Joint List and Ra’am, or the United Arab List.

Netanyahu’s camp has been accused of seeking to delegitimise the results after launching a series of largely discounted claims that the vote for the Arab parties, which scored their best-ever electoral performance, had been manipulated by foreign interference.

Despite their historic showing that was boosted by an unprecedented surge in voter turnout, the two Arab-led lists remain politically isolated. And while there have been indications that they would be prepared to support, or at least not oppose, an Eisenkot-led government, their backing remains contentious within the opposition – a broad and increasingly fractious alliance that also includes parties led by former Prime Ministers Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid, left-winger Yair Golan and right-winger Avigdor Lieberman.

After a meeting on Tuesday, the main opposition leaders issued a statement announcing that they were preparing to “act immediately” to replace Netanyahu’s governing coalition “with a national emergency government and translate the clear parliamentary majority in the Knesset into action”. Yet, the statement did not specify how they would reach the majority that would ultimately depend on them allying with either the Arab-led lists or two ultra-Orthodox parties, which have historically supported Netanyahu in return for shielding some of their members from military service.

“Essentially, we’re both on track to a government, and nowhere near being able to form one,” Israeli pollster Mitchell Barak told Al Jazeera.

Though informal negotiations are widely reported to have begun, official talks on establishing a governing coalition will start only after the results are certified on Wednesday. Netanyahu’s Likud party has already mooted refusing to recognise the results, citing its continuing claims of irregularities in the Arab vote. Those allegations have been investigated and discounted by police, while a separate probe by the internal security service, the Shin Bet, remains ongoing.

Once the results are certified, President Isaac Herzog will begin consultations with all the parties to determine which member of the Knesset, not necessarily a party leader, is best placed to form a government.

Herzog, who lost to Netanyahu after an especially bitter contest in 2015, has found himself in the unusual position of having to decide who should be given the first opportunity to form a government, while simultaneously considering the prime minister’s longstanding request for a pardon in his ongoing corruption trial .

One of Herzog’s options is to ask the Arab parties to recommend Eisenkot. If selected, the leader of the centrist Yashar party will initially have 28 days to assemble a coalition, a period that can be extended by 14 days. Should he fail, Herzog can then invite another candidate to try.

For his part, Netanyahu on Monday argued that Likud’s first-place finish, with 27 seats, gave him a mandate to lead the next government. “We aim to form a broad government with our partners and with any other party that wishes to join, provided they do not support terrorism,” he said.

Still, it is unlikely he will be able to command a majority without entering an alliance with the Arab parties that he has consistently vilified, or a large-scale wave of defections from the opposition.

Whatever the state of the negotiations, the new Knesset is due to be sworn in on November 10.

Barak said coordination within the opposition appeared minimal, while personal animosities between Netanyahu and Herzog further complicated already fraught negotiations.

“It’s really not clear who’s talking to who,” he added.

“Earlier this week, they named [Bennett’s running mate] Lapid as their choice of speaker, which was apparently news to both Eisenkot and Bennett. Equally, Netanyahu now has to appeal to his political rival, Herzog, both to be given the responsibility of forming a government and to be pardoned before any conviction,” Barak continued.

“All the while, he’s claiming that the Arab parties cannot be considered legitimate partners in government, which makes it almost impossible for anyone to form a coalition with them.”

However, the extent to which the efforts to delegitimise the Arab parties may succeed remains uncertain. Ra’am served as a central plank of the Bennett-Lapid coalition in 2021–22, the first time an independent Arab party had formally joined an Israeli government, with public pressure to do so again growing.

Over the weekend , thousands rallied in Tel Aviv calling upon Eisenkot to make a deal with the Arab parties that reflected the overwhelming number of votes cast against Netanyahu’s governing coalition. However, following the meeting between the opposition leaders on Tuesday, sources within the Joint List told Al Jazeera they were not expecting to be invited to support the bloc anytime soon.

Instead, speculation has turned to the possibility of one of the two ultra-Orthodox parties – Shas and United Torah Judaism (UTJ), and particularly the latter – defecting to the opposition and backing Eisenkot.

Neither Shas nor UTJ have had straightforward relationships with Netanyahu’s governing coalition. In fact, it was the withdrawal of their parliamentary support in May, following what they saw as the coalition’s failure to pass a draft law exempting some of their ultra-Orthodox members from military service, that fundamentally weakened its majority in parliament.

“There are rumours that the Ashkenazi [Jews, who make up the bulk of the UTJ membership] are ready to break with Netanyahu and go to Eisenkot,” political analyst Nimrod Flaschenberg told Al Jazeera.

“I am sceptical, but even that would still leave them short of an overall majority, so they would still need support from one of the Arab parties, even if that is Ra’am supporting them from outside a formal coalition,” he said of the parliamentary arithmetic.

Hanging over all, however, are developments tied to Israel’s deep and longstanding alliance with the United States.

Barak said the entire government-formation process risked being disrupted by the results of Tuesday’s midterm elections in the US, which could weaken Israel’s foremost ally, President Donald Trump, or be overtaken entirely by renewed war with Iran.

Netanyahu, particularly, went to pains during the election campaign to stress his relationship with Trump, whose Republican Party faces a tough race to keep hold of Congress.

Equally, both Trump’s rhetoric as well as the renewed build-up of US forces in the region may all signal the beginning of renewed conflict with Israel’s regional nemesis, Iran.

“Netanyahu cannot form a coalition,” Yossi Mekelberg, a senior fellow at Chatham House, told Al Jazeera. “It’s a numbers game, and he just doesn’t have the numbers – no amount of talking and planning can change that, but an emergency could, and in Israel, there’s no more popular an emergency than one involving Iran.”

In such an instance, he speculated that the incumbent could ask the opposition to fall in behind him, but that would raise the possibility of a former captain dictating war policy to former generals.

“There’s also the possibility that, however you want to define it, Israel has a successful war against Iran. That leads to a surge in popularity for Netanyahu when negotiations on a coalition resume, or [him] calling unnecessary, fresh elections,” said Mekelberg.

He was very understanding of it.”The current assistance framework dates to 2016, when then-President Barack Obama signed a 10-year security agreement committing the US to provide Israel with $38 billion in military aid, equivalent to $3.8 billion annually. Under the arrangement, Israel's ability to spend part of the funds on its own military products was to be phased out, with the money eventually directed entirely towards American defence industries.Netanyahu has previously spoken about reducing Israel's dependence on US assistance. In an interview with The Economist in January, he said he wanted to “taper off” American military aid over the next 10 years, adding that such a change was “in the works”. In October, he also said Israel should prepare for the eventual end of US aid.Netanyahu has also spoken about the need for Israel to move away from American military assistance. In October, he said the country should prepare for the end of US aid, even as formal discussions on a successor to the current agreement remain under way.The US has obligations under the Camp David peace accords with Egypt to provide security assistance to both Israel and Egypt. Much of the funding to Israel also comes through foreign military financing, which requires the country to spend the money on American-produced weapons. A reduction in such assistance could therefore affect US defence contractors unless Israel continues purchasing comparable amounts of American military equipment.You use AI every day. articles.title: King calls slave trade a 'shameful chapter' during Commonwealth address
articles.summary: The speech comes after calls for the UK government to issue a formal apology for Britain's historic role in the trade.
articles.body:
King Charles has described the transatlantic slave trade as a "shameful chapter of history" that filled him with "profound sorrow" as he opened a summit of Commonwealth leaders in the Caribbean.

He said the trade in enslaved persons "still casts a shadow" over the association of nations.

There have been calls from some for the UK to make a formal apology for its historic role in the slave trade ahead of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (Chogm) in Antigua and Barbuda, but there was not one in the King's address.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham, also at the summit, has said that he is open to Britain issuing a formal apology but has ruled out financial reparations.

While there was no direct apology, the King did offer some contrition - and there was also an acknowledgement that he had personally learnt more about the legacy of the slave trade.

He said: "The transatlantic trade in enslaved persons still casts a shadow over these islands and other members of our Commonwealth.

"As I have said before, that shameful chapter of history is one that fills my heart with horror and my soul with the most profound personal sorrow."

He told the summit: "The more I have furthered my own understanding of the issues, through listening, learning and looking, the more committed I have become to finding ways for us to work in modern partnership to address the wrongs of the past with action for the future."

King Charles continued: "History is not ours to choose or to change. It is bequeathed to us in complex synthesis by forebears we can never know.

"Our inheritance includes both their achievements and their failures – the good they did as well as the wrongs."

The King's address also referenced the "brutal conflicts" the world is facing, the "catastrophic reality" of climate and rapid technological development.

The Chogm meeting gathers leaders from 56 states every two years in a different part of the Commonwealth, a voluntary grouping made up primarily of former territories of the British Empire.

The biennial meeting's official theme this year is Accelerating Partnerships and Investment for a Prosperous Commonwealth.

Speaking on Tuesday, Burnham said his government was bringing a new approach, aiming to "revitalise the Commonwealth", despite turning down demands for reparations.

"I've been very clear that we do not support reparations," he said.

"But it's not the case that we don't support countries in the Commonwealth around development, and helping them with debt issues that they've got, green finance.

"That's what we've done under all governments and in my view we should continue to do as part of being a Commonwealth."

The King and Queen are on a tour of the Caribbean which has reignited difficult debates over the UK's colonial legacy in the region.

On his first stop in the Bahamas, the King delivered a speech in which he spoke of the "suffering of the past".

In Guyana, he visited the site of a Slave Rebellion, where hundreds of enslaved people were killed.

articles.title: Democratic wave, Republican resilience or gridlock? Three ways US midterms could play out
articles.summary: After months of campaigning and billions of dollars spent, election day in the US midterms has arrived.
articles.body: After months of campaigning and billions of dollars spent, election day in the US midterms has arrived. Public opinion polls give Democrats an edge, but past elections show polls are not always reliable, reports BBC News.History shows midterm elections usually favour the party out of power. Factors such as low presidential approval ratings, high consumer costs linked to the war with Iran, and debated policies on immigration and data centre construction have set the stage. As votes are counted, three main outcomes could shape the future of Congress.Scenario 1: A big Democratic waveIn this outcome, momentum pushes Democrats far beyond simple control of the House of Representatives, past the 218 seats needed for a majority. They win toss-up contests and flip seats in conservative strongholds.In the Senate, Democrats take most toss-up races and secure victories in traditionally Republican states like Texas or Kansas. This cushion prevents complications from legal challenges, such as the dispute in Alaska regarding two candidates named Dan Sullivan on the ballot.This result relies on strong Democratic turnout, winning independent voters, and reversing previous Republican gains among Hispanic voters and young men. An outcome like this would give Democrats legislative control and lead to two years of intense confrontation with US President Donald Trump.Early indicators include Democrats holding target seats in Florida, gaining House districts in states like North Carolina, Michigan, New York, Virginia, and Kentucky, or winning the Senate race in South Carolina.Scenario 2: A Democratic trickleIn this outcome, Democrats win the House with a narrow majority. Leaders must balance votes between progressive and moderate factions to pass legislation.In the Senate, Democrats pick up limited seats, such as North Carolina, but fail to win in conservative states. Incumbents like Republican Senator Susan Collins in Maine retain their seats, Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed falls short in Michigan, or the ballot dispute in Alaska impacts Democratic candidate Mary Peltola.This happens if high Democratic early voting is matched by strong Republican turnout on election day, resulting in a divided Congress and legislative gridlock.Early indicators include Florida remaining comfortably Republican while Democrats make limited House gains in Virginia and Pennsylvania without sweeping broader seats.Scenario 3: A good night for RepublicansIn this outcome, Republicans maintain control of both chambers of Congress. This requires polling errors that underestimated support for Donald Trump, alongside strong Republican, independent, and Hispanic voter turnout.Control of the House could hinge on extended vote counting in California. favourable redistricting in states such as Texas, Florida, and North Carolina would help Republicans secure a slim majority. In the Senate, Republicans hold conservative states and flip Democratic seats like Michigan.This result allows Trump to claim an electoral mandate and proceed with his domestic and foreign policy agenda alongside a Republican-led Congress.Early indicators include solid re-election wins for Senators Ashley Moody in Florida and Jon Husted in Ohio, alongside Republican House gains in North Carolina, Ohio, and Florida.What is at stake across the countryVoters will decide all 435 House seats, 35 Senate races, and 36 governorships across the country. Heading into election day, Republicans hold slim majorities in both chambers, sitting at 218 House seats and 53 in the Senate. Democrats need to net just four seats in each chamber to flip control. Because of those narrow margins, the fight for Capitol Hill will come down to roughly 47 toss-up House districts and 11 competitive Senate races.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.body: Iran's senior security official Mohsen Rezaei has claimed that Pakistan Army chief Asim Munir warned of growing ties between Hindus and Jews, alleging that the emerging partnership posed a threat to Pakistan and the wider Muslim world.In an interview with Iranian state media, Rezaei said Munir raised concerns over growing India-Israel ties during a four-nation security meeting in Tehran on October 26. Mr Asim Munir also spoke about the threat posed by Israel and the emerging bond between Hindus and Jews against Muslims and even Pakistan. These remarks reflect their information and concerns about how Israel may act towards them in the future," he added.Munir has repeatedly invoked religious differences between Hindus and Muslims, describing the two communities as fundamentally distinct.Days before the Pakistan-backed Pahalgam terror attack in April 2025, Munir had spoken about the differences between Hindus and Muslims in their religion, customs, traditions, thoughts and ambitions. He had also invoked the Two-Nation Theory.While Rezaei's latest account of Munir's remarks remains unverified, the reported comments are consistent with the Pakistani army chief's earlier rhetoric.Meanwhile, India and Israel have steadily expanded cooperation across defence, intelligence, counterterrorism, trade, agriculture, water management and emerging technologies. articles.title: Action needed to tackle Jersey's 'biodiversity crisis'
articles.summary: The issue is part of wider concerns the government is not focused enough on the environment.
articles.body:
A scrutiny panel has heard Jersey is in a "biodiversity crisis", amid concerns the government is not focusing on the environment enough.

Willie Peggie, government Director of Natural Environment, said the Environment Department needed time and resources for a state of nature report.

Piers Sangan, who runs Sangan Island Conversation, said a biodiversity crisis included more invasive species, fewer native species, and a decline in the ecosystem. He said the government had responsibility to ensure the environment did not "fall by the wayside" because it was a "fundamental part of our island".

The environment minister said policies were being worked on to further protect the environment.

Peggie said any state of nature report should be similar to those in the UK , Guernsey and Alderney .

Sangan said Jersey's biodiversity strategy had been "put on the shelf" since the early 2000s, and the island had lost animals including stoats.

He said there had been a "woeful lack of investment" in ecology.

"The environment is becoming quieter and, as someone who's been looking at this day in, day out for the last 15 years, it's becoming horribly noticeable."

He said several bird species were struggling to increase numbers.

"Even though they're still here, they're still breeding, they're not increasing in number... They are more or less extinct already and are likely to go extinct in the next few years," he said.

Environment Minister Senator Mary Le Hegarat said the countryside needed to be managed properly with a rise in invasive species.

She said: "Everybody needs to manage the countryside together, and we'll do the work and set out the policies and strategies in order to do so."

Government officials are expected to release a state of nature report in 2027, which would inform a new biodiversity strategy.

Joshua and Benjamin Voak work for the Jersey Grazing Project, which uses cows and sheep to improve and restore habitats.

Joshua Voak said it was concerning the environment had not been discussed much in the summer's election as "there are so many economic advantages to having a healthy environment".

Benjamin said biodiversity was "super important" for the island's air and water quality and the retention of habitats.

Concerns around biodiversity come as questions have been raised about the government's commitment to the environment.

Deputy Hilary Jeune, who chairs the environment scrutiny panel, said ministers' draft Common Strategic Policy did not take the natural environment into account.

The panel worked with Le Hegarat on an amendment to address that .

Jeune said biodiversity needed to be "front and centre".

Professor Liz Bentley was part of the Jersey Climate Council, which suggested Jersey need to spend £10m per year to reach net zero by 2050, rather than the £4m in the Climate Emergency Fund.

She said the council recognised the financial pressure on the government, but delayed action to tackle climate change would cost more in the long-term.

"We need to consider it over decades, not over a four year budget... It's about that long-term investment."

Le Hegarat said ministers needed to be "very cautious" about spending.

She could not say how much it would cost to reach net zero by 2050, but thought investing the money in the fund was a good way forward.

articles.title: US midterms 2026: Could a Trump defeat in Congress alter the Iran war?
articles.summary: The outcome of the US midterm elections could reshape the political constraints on US president Donald Trump’s war with Iran, even if it does not directly
articles.body: The outcome of the US midterm elections could reshape the political constraints on US president Donald Trump’s war with Iran, even if it does not directly determine the course of the military campaign.A Democratic takeover of the House of Representatives would give the opposition greater power to investigate the administration’s handling of the conflict, question its objectives and press for limits on further military action. But Trump would remain commander-in-chief, with the authority to direct US military operations.Congress does have powers over war and military spending, but using them to force a president to change course is difficult. Trump could veto legislation seeking to restrict military operations, and overriding that veto would require a two-thirds majority in both chambers, a threshold Democrats are unlikely to reach even if they make significant gains. Lawmakers may also be reluctant to cut funding for American troops already deployed in the region.The political pressure could nevertheless influence Trump's calculations. The Iran war has become a domestic issue as its economic consequences, particularly rising energy prices and the cost of living, weigh on voters. A recent survey cited by the Washington Examiner found that more than 70% of Americans wanted Congress to prioritise lowering living costs and ending the war in 2027. Discontent has also emerged within Trump's MAGA base, where opposition to overseas military involvement has challenged his earlier “America First” promises.There are also questions over whether the administration could resume or expand military action after the elections. NPR reported that US and Israeli preparations for a possible renewed round of attacks have fuelled expectations of escalation after the midterms. The US has two aircraft carriers in the Arabian Sea, with a third on the way, while US allies in the region have stepped up military exercises. These developments do not confirm that an attack is imminent, but point to the possibility of a wider campaign.Trump could therefore face three broad paths after the vote: pull back and seek a negotiated settlement, maintain the current pressure through the blockade and targeted strikes, or escalate the campaign against Iran and its regional allies. The election result may alter the political costs of each option, but the most consequential decisions will remain with the White House.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.summary: Richard Wilkins, 62, from Swindon, is one of four men on trial at Winchester Crown Court.
articles.body:
A man accused of raping a woman after he answered an advert for sex online said he was told she would "pretend to be asleep" by her then husband.

Richard Wilkins, 62, is one of four men accused of sexual offences against Joanne Young, who was drugged and raped by Philip Young over 13 years at their Swindon home.

Giving evidence, Wilkins said he was told to "come in, have sex and leave" after answering a Craigslist post in 2016 that he thought was placed by the couple but was actually placed by Young alone .

Wilkins is on trial with Norman Macksoni, 48, Connor Sanderson-Doyle, 32, and Mohammed Hassan, 38. They all deny sexual offences against Joanne, who was waived her right to anonymity.

Wilkins, of Toothill in Swindon, who worked as a taxi driver in the town at the time, has pleaded not guilty to one count of rape and one of assault by penetration.

He told the court he had responded to an ad that he believed was from "a couple looking for another guy".

Recalling what the advert said, Wilkins told Winchester Crown Court: "It was something about one of her fantasies is to be tied and blindfolded, and for this to work properly for her it should be anonymous."

Wilkins said he also remembered being told by Young that his wife might be drunk.

"I remember saying it wouldn't be much fun if she's pissed. [Young] said maybe she has had a drink, she pretends to sleep and if you get her going she might respond," he told the court.

Before attending the couple's home, Wilkins said he had sent two photos of himself, after Young said his wife requested it.

Wilkins said he had asked to speak to Joanne during a phone call prior to the incident, but Young told him she was busy and had said to tell him "she's looking forward to having you".

"I said, 'would you rather us meet for a drink?'. [Young] said no," Wilkins told the court.

The defendant said he had got the impression the Youngs "seemed endearing, like it was genuine".

"The impression I got, he was very confident about it, that they had a lot of experience, it was something they were comfortable doing it, they were happy doing it," he added.

The court previously heard Young had placed 20 adverts on Craigslist inviting men to have sex with his wife. He also posted on other sites, including Grindr and Fab Swingers.

One advert said the idea was to "quietly use her body" and that "even a voice would be a giveaway" to the person's identity, the jury heard.

The court was previously told the investigation into Young was launched after police were alerted to the fact he had uploaded extreme pornographic images to the internet in 2023.

Searches of his devices found nearly 500 images of Joanne "in a state of undress", with the majority "not with knowledge or consent".

Young has admitted 48 offences against his ex-wife, including voyeurism, rape, administering a substance with intent, assault by penetration and sexual assault.

He also pleaded guilty to three charges of making indecent images of children, one of possessing prohibited images of children, and four of possessing an extreme pornographic image.

A sixth defendant, Dean Hamilton, 47, of Street, Somerset, has admitted one charge of assault by penetration, two of sexual assault and one of rape.

Young and Hamilton will be sentenced at the end of the trial.

articles.title: Melania Trump to host Russia, Ukraine officials at White House over Oleshky ceasefire
articles.summary: US first lady Melania Trump will host representatives from Russia and Ukraine at the White House on Thursday to discuss a recently concluded ceasefire and
articles.body: US first lady Melania Trump will host representatives from Russia and Ukraine at the White House on Thursday to discuss a recently concluded ceasefire and humanitarian operation in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky, the White House announced on Tuesday.The six-day truce, which ended on November 1, allowed emergency aid to reach the town and enabled civilians to leave for Ukrainian-controlled territory or Russia. Melania Trump is scheduled to deliver remarks on the operation at 11 am EST. The White House did not identify the representatives invited to attend.A Ukrainian official told The Kyiv Independent that Ukraine’s human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets and Russia’s human rights commissioner Yana Lantratova are expected to be present. However, Lantratova is under US sanctions imposed in 2022 and would require a special waiver from the State Department to enter the country. A spokesperson for Lubinets declined to comment to the publication.The White House described the ceasefire as an initiative independently pursued by Melania Trump, saying she had engaged with the two countries and secured a truce in Oleshky and the surrounding Kherson region. The first lady called the operation a success and said nearly 800 people had been evacuated, although neither Kyiv nor Moscow has publicly confirmed the number or the destinations of those who left.The announcement follows a Le Monde report that the humanitarian operation had been negotiated over four months by Russia’s GRU and Ukraine’s HUR military intelligence agencies. Citing sources, the French newspaper reported that the two sides had agreed to credit Melania Trump with the ceasefire to appease US president Donald Trump as he seeks a breakthrough in peace negotiations.Oleshky has been under Russian occupation since 2022. Reports suggest conditions in the town deteriorated in mid-2026, with residents facing shortages of food, drinking water, electricity and medical supplies, while Russian forces effectively prevented humanitarian organisations from delivering aid. Under international humanitarian law, Russia is responsible for protecting civilians in territory under its occupation.The Kremlin has publicly ruled out further humanitarian operations of this kind in the foreseeable future. Meanwhile, Russia and the US have confirmed that trilateral talks aimed at ending the war will resume in Abu Dhabi on November 10 and 11. The negotiations had stalled in February amid the conflict in the Middle East.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Trump celebrates early Republican gains in Guam, says ‘hopefully that’s an indication’ for US midterms
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump has welcomed Republican gains in Guam's gubernatorial election, congratulating Republican candidate Tony Ada and suggesting the
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has welcomed Republican gains in Guam's gubernatorial election, congratulating Republican candidate Tony Ada and suggesting the result could signal wider gains for his party in the November 3 US midterm elections.“Guam, which has always been considered strongly Democrat, just had an early call for a REPUBLICAN Victory in the top spot, Governor — Congratulations to Tony Ada!” Trump wrote in a post on his Truth Social platform.He also claimed that Republicans had secured a majority in Guam's legislature and added: “Wow, hopefully that’s an indication for things to come!”According to the unofficial tally reported by local media, Ada and Calvo received 15,945 votes, or 51.45%, against 14,925 votes, or 48.15%, for Terlaje and Perez. The results are subject to certification by the Guam Election Commission.The Republican's unofficial victory came alongside another significant development for the party in Guam's local politics. Republicans secured eight of the 15 seats in the territory's legislature, compared with seven won by Democrats, according to Public Radio Guam. Democrats flip Guam's congressional seat: Unofficial resultThe gubernatorial gain was not the only major outcome of the election. Democrat Alicia Limtiaco defeated Republican incumbent James Moylan in the contest for Guam's delegate to the US House of Representatives.Limtiaco, a former attorney general of Guam, received 15,645 votes, or 51%, compared with Moylan's 14,983 votes, or 48.84%, according to the final unofficial tally reported by The Wall Street Journal.Moylan had won the seat in 2024 with 52.7% of the vote. Limtiaco's lead therefore represents a Democratic gain in the territory's congressional representation.However, Guam's delegate to the House does not have a vote on final passage of legislation on the House floor. The seat does not affect the balance of power between Republicans and Democrats in the chamber.Phillip Tydingco also defeated incumbent attorney general Doug Moylan in another key contest, according to Public Radio Guam.Why the Guam result mattersGuam is an unincorporated US territory in the western Pacific. Its residents are US citizens but cannot vote in the US presidential general election. They elect their own governor and a delegate to the US House, who can participate in House proceedings but cannot vote on final passage of legislation.The territory has a 15-member unicameral legislature, whose members are commonly called senators. Therefore, Trump's reference to a Republican majority in the "State Senate" was referring to the Republican majority in Guam's territorial legislature, not a separate state Senate.The outgoing governor, Democrat Lou Leon Guerrero, was term-limited and could not seek another term. Ada's victory ends the Democrats' eight-year hold on the governorship.The election produced a mixed outcome: Republicans won the governorship and a legislative majority, while Democrats captured Guam's congressional delegate seat.The Guam Election Commission's results remain unofficial. The commission's tentative schedule provides for the final tabulation and certification on November 19, after absentee ballots are received.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Yemen gov’t accuses IRGC, Hezbollah of sending 21 experts to back Houthis
articles.summary: Yemeni interior minister says foreign involvement expanded beyond arms and training to directing military operations.
articles.body:
Yemen’s internationally recognised government has accused Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), as well as Lebanon’s Hezbollah, of deploying 21 experts to help the Houthis plan and direct military operations in the country.

Interior Minister Major-General Ibrahim Haidan said in a statement on Tuesday that 14 members of the group are from the IRGC and seven from Hezbollah.

The experts’ roles show that foreign involvement has moved from financing, arming and training to “direct supervision and participation in planning and managing operations and building military capabilities”, said Haidan.

The statement added that eight of the experts are in Hodeidah, four in Sanaa, four in Saada, two in Hajjah, two in Amran and one in the coastal city of Khokha.

It listed their specialities as including command and control, ballistic missiles and drones, electronic warfare, smuggling military components, coordinating naval operations and choosing commercial ships as targets , developing explosive-laden boats and autonomous submarines, and training fighters in mine-laying and siege tactics.

Haidan warned that the activities “threaten shipping in the Bab al-Mandeb strait and the Red Sea” and could transfer military expertise to other armed groups.

He called on the international community to designate the Houthis a “terrorist” organisation, dismantle their financing and arms networks, and enforce the arms embargo under United Nations Security Council resolutions 2216 and 2624.

The statement comes as Yemeni armed forces and fighters loyal to the government battle the Houthis in five provinces, after the group seized the western Red Sea coast and the Bab al-Mandeb area in September.

The resumption of fighting has shattered a relative quiet brought by a 2022 ceasefire that followed a lengthy civil war which first erupted in 2014, when the Houthis seized the capital, Sanaa.

In 2015, Saudi Arabia entered the war at the head of an international coalition aimed at restoring Yemen’s internationally recognised government.

The government has long claimed the IRGC is supporting the Houthis, while Tehran insists the Houthis act independently. The Houthis acknowledge their alliance with Iran but have long denied being an Iranian proxy, while Hezbollah has previously rejected having a role in Yemen’s war.

Saudi Arabia, whose airports and oil facilities have come under Houthi attack in recent weeks, has accused Iran of encouraging the escalation.

articles.title: A Los Angeles artist bought an 1888 Victorian house in 1979 and turned it purple inside and out; now the estate is on the market, asking $2 million for the four-bedroom property, with restoration estimated to cost at least $1 million
articles.summary: A ‘unicorn’ Los Angeles house has hit the market, asking $2 million, according to a listing on Coldwell Banker Realty.
articles.body: A ‘unicorn’ Los Angeles house has hit the market, asking $2 million, according to a listing on Coldwell Banker Realty. Built in 1888, this purple-drenched Queen Anne Victorian is a rare piece of the city's history. Known as Esperanza House, the 2,700-square-foot property sits on half an acre. The 138-year-old house on the hill is hard to miss, thanks to its purple hue.A rare survivorThe unicorn house is a rare survivor, according to the listing agent, Laurie Turner, of Coldwell Banker Residential Brokerage in Pasadena. “Los Angeles doesn’t have a lot of 138-year-old houses anymore,” she told Realtor.com. “Los Angeles was a big agricultural zone, and people were coming out west for opportunity and land and things that they didn't have on the East Coast and in the Midwest.”Turner calls Esperanza House a unicorn. The home was built in 1888. “It was the 1880s and the height of the Industrial Revolution. A world of knowledge and ideas was rapidly unfolding, mixing old and new, foreign and familiar. European design ideas were embraced wholly and without reserve. Transportation technology improved and expanded at a fantastic rate, opening the door to the West to people from all around the globe. Factories utilising recent advances in industrial technology were turning out mass-produced goods at prices affordable to the growing 'middle class'. This, combined with the great Southern California Land Boom of the 1880s, resulted in a proliferation of elaborate and eclectic architecture throughout Los Angeles, as demonstrated here,” the listing says, describing the house's unique look.The house was yellow before becoming purpleWhen Leonora Pierotti Thomas bought the house in 1979, it was yellow. Turner, who never met Thomas, has heard stories from her cousin, who said that nearly everything about her was purple. “It was yellow when Leonora bought it, and from what I hear from her cousin, everything about [Leonora] was purple. She drove a purple Hummer. The garden hoses were purple. I have a picture that was sent out in memory [of her], and she is with her poodle and she had dyed her poodle’s fur purple,” the agent recalled.She added, “She was an eccentric artist, never married, [who] had the wherewithal to have a home like this, travel the world, entertain. I've heard stories. I unfortunately never had the opportunity to meet her, but she just sounds like a kick.”Inside the purple houseThe four-bedroom, three-bathroom house also has a fireplace. The purple does not stop at the front door. It covers the outside walls and the roof, which is newer and has purple trim. Inside, the kitchen island, some of the lights and several walls are purple too. Wooden flooring runs throughout the house. The kitchen and primary suite were added in the past ten years. According to the listing, the kitchen has been updated with a microwave, refrigerator, tankless water heater, dishwasher and electric cooktop.“I just love it. It’s such a happy place to be and it's warm and inviting… and although a little dilapidated right now, you can see what it was when Leonora was living there,” Turner told the outlet.The house needs workWhile the house is certainly unique, Turner is not hiding the work it needs. Some of the plaster is peeling off the walls. Turner says everything still functions, including the pool. “I'm calling it a historic restoration project rather than a fixer because fixer sounds like a fix and flip,” the agent said. She also revealed that the contractor she consulted estimated that the restoration work would cost at least $1 million. “I'm really looking [for a buyer] who has the vision and the wherewithal to update the home, bring it back to its glory, live in it, and do right by the neighbours and the neighbourhood.”Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: A Long Island family used a rare Ming dynasty vase’s wooden stand as a doorstop; the vase later sold at auction for $1.3 million
articles.summary: A Long Island family unknowingly used a rare Ming dynasty vase as a doorstop for decades, only to discover its value when it sold for $1.3 million at auction. This article delves into the fascinating history of Ming dynasty ceramics and the auction that exceeded all expectations.
articles.body: The odds of finding a relic from ancient history amid one’s home seem to be a near-impossible fluke. But for a family in a Long Island home, that far-fetched idea was no mere happenstance; rather, it became a reality. For decades, a rare Chinese vase sat on a wooden stand that the family used as a doorstop.The vase, a blue and white moonflask, had a lineage that dated back to China’s Ming dynasty. According to the BBC, the moonflask went on to sell for more than $1.3 million at Sotheby’s New York auction in September 2012, against a pre-sale estimate of $600,000. The Associated Press reported that its owners eventually reconsidered the object after seeing a similar piece in an advertisement for Sotheby’s.Chinese ceramics during the Ming DynastyThe moonflask came from a period when Chinese ceramics and porcelain were sought after by collectors from China and overseas alike. The World Civilisation chapter on the Ming Dynasty identifies ceramic art as the zeitgeist of the period’s prominent form of artistic production. At the time, its major porcelain production centres were located in the imperial kilns at Jingdezhen in Jiangxi province and the factories at Dehua in Fujian.Dehua manufacturers were producing porcelain that catered to European buyers by the 16th century. Historian Chuimei Ho estimated that roughly 16% of late Ming-era Chinese ceramic exports, according to her study of the ceramic trade, were bound for Europe, while the remainder headed to Japan and Southeast Asia. The acquisition of porcelain during that time was a privilege exclusive to affluent households, where it was displayed in tandem with silks, jade, ivory and cloisonne. That demand helped make a Ming moonflask like this one a prized object. This widespread practice backed a robust market ecosystem that supported dealers and specialists.This boon, while benefiting legitimate dealers, also made room for counterfeiters. The World Civilisation account records that imitation objects and false attributions circulated during the late Ming period. It notes that counterfeiters profited from this trade. Liu Tong, whose book was printed in 1635, provided guidance for collectors attempting to distinguish authentic objects from imitations. Examining the sheen of bronzework could authenticate work from the Xuande era (1426–1435), while the thickness of porcelain would validate work from the Yongle era (1402–1424).Other objects at Sotheby’s New York auctionThe moonflask wasn’t the only coveted object offered at Sotheby’s Chinese works of art sale in New York on 11 and 12 September 2012. According to the BBC, the auction raised nearly $27 million, exceeding its pre-sale projection of $21.6 million. The total was almost 20% higher than the equivalent sale just a year before.Another lot displayed a Wucai fish jar and cover previously owned by the Walters Art Museum in Baltimore. It sold for nearly $3.5 million, with the proceeds intended to benefit the museum’s Asian Art Acquisitions Fund. The auction also included a pair of 17th-century armchairs that had been given to a church in Victoria, Canada, which the Associated Press reported had been used by clergy and members of the congregation before selling for $758,500.Dr Tao Wang, who had been appointed head of Sotheby’s Chinese Works of Art Department, commented on the results. Speaking after the auction, he said: "We saw exceptional demand across the sale, which drove the total to such heights." By his account, collectors from around the world had been drawn to the high-calibre artefacts owing to their distinguished provenance.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Mary Kay Ash invested her $5,000 life savings to start a Dallas cosmetics company; after her husband died before its launch, her son took over the administrative work
articles.summary: Discover how Mary Kay Ash turned her $5,000 savings into a global cosmetics brand after the tragic loss of her husband just before launch. Explore her groundbreaking business model that empowered women and broke barriers in the cosmetics industry.
articles.body: In business, founders can often lose partners, suppliers, and financing, but very few dare to rebuild everything, especially after losing the person who stood with them through every moment. Something similar happened with Mary Kay Ash. After her husband died of a heart attack, Ash went ahead with her plan anyway. On 13 September 1963, she opened Beauty by Mary Kay with $5,000 of her life savings, her 20-year-old son, Richard Rogers, and nine independent beauty consultants, according to the company’s press kit. Her business began in a 500-square-foot storefront in Dallas and is now sold in more than 35 markets around the world.How the business workedAsh did not step into the system without having any knowledge. She spent most of her career in direct sales, starting as a dealer for Stanley Home Products, a firm built on home parties, according to the Horatio Alger Association. At that firm, she was named ‘Queen of Sales’ after her first year. In the 1950s, she became national training director at another direct sales company, World Gift. The sticking point was that she kept training young men who were then promoted over her. By early 1963, she had retired with the idea of writing a book to help women build careers in business.Shift in the projectWhile planning the book, Ash made two lists, one covering what her former employers had done well and the other covering what they could have done better. After making the list and analysing it, she realised that she had accidentally created a marketing plan for a company of her own, where one woman could earn as far as their efforts would carry them. And that's how the book turned into a business plan. She put her $5,000 into the project and used it to buy formulas for skin care products and pay to have them bottled and packaged for shipping. Then came the launch part, which was quite hard to implement.The darkest day Her husband died even before the launch of the business they were both working on. The Horatio Alger Association, which also praised Ash with their award, noted that he was meant to run the administration. Ash was quite affected by the death of her husband and later labelled that day as the darkest day of her life. According to her autobiography, Mary Kay, her accountant and her lawyer both advised her to cancel everything she was working on. The advice seemed reasonable on paper because she was risking every dollar she had saved. Even through these obstacles, Ash didn’t give up, and her son Richard Rogers took over the administrative work his father had been due to handle. That’s how he also played a big role in growing the business.How the business grew Independent consultants bought products from the companies at a set wholesale price and sold them directly to customers at a justified retail price, which means that what each woman earned depended on how many leads she got and how much she was able to sell. A woman could start by buying a starter kit, but what she earned from there depended on her effort and circumstances, and individual results varied.Access to credit mattered too. In 1963, federal law did not stop lenders from turning applicants down because of their sex or marital status. That changed with the Equal Credit Opportunity Act, which was signed on 28 October 1974 and took effect on 28 October 1975, according to the Federal Reserve. When it put the law into practice, the Federal Reserve said the Act forbade creditors from discriminating on those grounds and covered banks, finance companies, department stores and credit card issuers. In the years before that, a selling model that a woman could join with a starter kit offered a way in that did not depend on a bank’s approval.Returns on investmentThe results were worth noticing. According to the company’s press kit, Mary Kay’s worldwide wholesale sales stand at $2.5 billion, and the company has been listed among the 100 best companies to work for in America several times, as the Horatio Alger Association notes.You use AI every day.
